ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105), ss 87A-87H (ultimate controller register), s 21 (company name requirements), s 189 (registered office); Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (Public Act 2009 No 35), ss 10-14 and ss 22-29 (customer due diligence, PEP and sanctions); Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (Definitions) Regulations 2011; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (Requirement to Verify Identity) Regulations 2011; United Nations Act 1946; Russia Sanctions Act 2022; Income Tax Act 2007.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Mutually exclusive path: (A) for a Hague Apostille Convention destination, notarize the certified copy if required and obtain an Apostille from the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (MFAT) Legalisation Unit only; (B) for a non-Apostille destination, notarize if required, obtain MFAT authentication, then obtain consular legalization from the destination state's embassy or consulate in New Zealand only. Never combine Apostille and consular legalization for the same document.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Compliance under section 32 Companies Act 1993
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Mutually exclusive path: (A) for a Hague Apostille Convention destination, notarize the certified copy if required and obtain a New Zealand MFAT Apostille only; (B) for a non-Apostille destination, notarize if required, obtain MFAT authentication, and then obtain consular legalization from the destination diplomatic mission in New Zealand only. Apostille and consular legalization are never applied to the same record.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution authorising incorporation and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand notary public authenticating the board resolution of NZ_LTD
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Mutually exclusive path: (A) for Hague Convention states, notarize the signatory's execution and affix the New Zealand MFAT Apostille; (B) for non-Hague states, notarize the execution, obtain MFAT authentication, and then have the destination embassy or consulate legalize the notarial certificate. These paths are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Constitution / Articles of Association of NZ_LTD
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: NZ_LTD adopted by shareholder resolution, certified by the New Zealand registered agent and notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Mutually exclusive path: (A) for a Hague Apostille destination, have the certified copy notarized and obtain a New Zealand MFAT Apostille; (B) for a non-Hague destination, have the certified copy notarized, obtain MFAT authentication, and then obtain consular legalization by the destination state's consular officer in New Zealand. Do not chain an Apostille after or before consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Existing relationship bank issuing the original signed bank reference on bank letterhead
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For consular filing, the original bank reference may be accepted without notarization; if foreign authorities require certification, use mutually exclusive path (A) notarize the bank officer's signature and obtain New Zealand MFAT Apostille for Hague states, or (B) notarize, obtain MFAT authentication, and then complete consular legalization at the destination embassy in New Zealand for non-Hague states.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening applies to every proposed director, shareholder/ultimate controller and authorised signatory before incorporation. Conduct identity verification and adverse media checks; screen against United Nations Security Council consolidated list, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, New Zealand consolidated sanctions lists and Russian/DPR/Ukraine regional sanctions under United Nations Act 1946 and Russia Sanctions Act 2022; screen against HM Treasury and EU sanctions where transactions use SWIFT/ACH rails. Identify foreign and domestic PEPs, family members and close associates using the AML/CFT Act definition; apply enhanced due diligence to PEPs and to any item linked to high-risk jurisdictions or shell banking flags. All results must be documented in a risk assessment report, retained for at least five years, and escalated through the AML/CFT compliance officer.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office - NZ Companies Register online portal (https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be registrable using the New Zealand Latin-script alphabet; macrons used for te reo Maori are permitted and consistently treated. Names in other scripts must be transliterated into a phonetically accurate Latin-script form and, where requested, a certified English translation must be supplied. The four-tier naming regime is: (1) full legal name reserved; (2) abbreviation/suffix tier, being Limited or Ltd; (3) alternate registered foreign-language name, if any; and (4) trading name or business brand, which must not be misleading or conflict with the Companies Register index.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may apply in writing to the Registrar of Companies for an objection decision under section 23 of the Companies Act 1993, specifying the proposed name, grounds, copy of rejection notice, evidence that the name is not misleading, offensive or contrary to law, and any existing user's consent. The Registrar must issue written reasons; if the objection is dismissed, an appeal may be filed with the District Court within 20 working days under section 24. If the reservation lapses, refile immediately before expiry and request no extension unless the Companies Office grants an administrative extension for pending court or agency approval.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Under Companies Act 1993, section 189, a New Zealand company must have a registered office that is a physical location in New Zealand, open to the public during business hours, and cannot be a P.O. Box. A virtual office service with a real street address and staff accepting service may satisfy strict legal registration, but Inland Revenue and AML-reporting banks generally reject a mailbox-only or corporate-agent-only address for this industry because it does not evidence commercial substance. For an ISO container leasing company with no local staff, acceptable substance requires a local director, physical registered office under service contract, maintained UBO register, adequate bank account, and financial records. A pure virtual mailbox is insufficient and will trigger enhanced bank scrutiny or refusal.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Inspection risk is Low (estimated less than 10% per annum) for a low-risk leasing holding vehicle with an engaged registered agent. Checklist: (1) ensure registered office sign/plate is displayed at the physical address; (2) maintain original minute book, constitution and UBO register at the registered office or agent; (3) maintain office rental/sublease and business records; (4) ensure the resident director and agent are contactable; and (5) complete annual return confirmation with the Companies Office. The risk rises to Moderate, approximately 25%, if a virtual mailbox is used without local substance, or if Inland Revenue, the Financial Intelligence Unit, or territorial authorities receive anomaly flags on turnover, tax filings, or banking transactions. Unannounced inspections by the Companies Office and Inland Revenue may occur in those cases.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), sections 12-16 (registration), 28-33 (constitution), 34-39 (share capital), 86-90 (share registers), 122-125 (board resolutions), 151-154 (directors), 180 (registered office)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Registrar of Companies
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form NZCO1 (Application for Registration of a Company) culminating in the Certificate of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Companies Act 1993 imposes no minimum paid-up capital requirement. A company can be incorporated with one share and no value fully issued and unpaid. The directors must maintain solvency and satisfy any contractual lender capital requirements; no blocked escrow account is mandated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY] LIMITED (COMPANY NUMBER [NUMBER]), DATED [DATE]. IN ACCORDANCE WITH SECTIONS 122 AND 125 OF THE COMPANIES ACT 1993 (NEW ZEALAND) AND THE CONSTITUTION OF THE COMPANY, THE DIRECTORS RESOLVE AS FOLLOWS. A. SHARE CAPITAL ALLOTMENT AND SUBSCRIPTION: 1. RESOLVED THAT the Company accepts the offer for subscription and allots and issues the ordinary shares as set forth in the allotment schedule, such shares ranking pari passu in all respects and being issued fully paid for consideration which the Board determines is reasonable under section 36(1) of the Companies Act 1993. 2. RESOLVED THAT the Board authorises the company secretary to execute share certificates and to complete and maintain the statutory share register pursuant to sections 86 and 90 of the Act. B. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: 3. RESOLVED THAT the Board hereby appoints [BANK NAME] as the Company's principal banker and authorises the operation of all corporate accounts in accordance with the approved banking mandate. 4. RESOLVED THAT any two directors, or one director together with the company secretary, are jointly authorised to sign cheques, draw and accept bills of exchange, execute promissory notes, and undertake electronic fund transfers, including SWIFT or ACH debits, subject to the transaction threshold that any transfer exceeding USD 100,000 requires dual signatures. C. REGISTERED OFFICE: 5. RESOLVED THAT the registered office of the Company be located at [ADDRESS], New Zealand, as the address for the service of documents pursuant to section 180 of the Companies Act 1993. 6. RESOLVED THAT the Board appoint [AGENT NAME] as the registered office contact agent with the authority to accept service of process on the Company's behalf. D. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS: 7. RESOLVED THAT [DIRECTOR A] and [DIRECTOR B] are hereby appointed as directors of the Company effective immediately, each having submitted their signed consent to act; [DIRECTOR A] is a resident of New Zealand for the purposes of section 151 of the Act. 8. RESOLVED THAT [SECRETARY NAME] be and is hereby appointed as the Company Secretary, with responsibility for maintaining the statutory registers, filing of annual returns, and supervising the company's compliance calendar. E. GENERAL PROVISIONS: 9. RESOLVED THAT the directors be and are hereby jointly and severally authorised to execute all ancillary applications, engage legal and accounting advisors, and incur such costs as may be necessary to implement these resolutions. 10. RESOLVED THAT this resolution may be executed in counterparts and takes effect as a resolution passed at a board meeting held in accordance with the company's constitution and the Companies Act 1993. DATED this [DATE]. SIGNED: [SECRETARY NAME] (Secretary) and [DIRECTOR NAME] (Director).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Submission of Incorporation Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office - online register via RealMe
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a name search on the Companies Register to verify the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing company under section 22 of the Companies Act 1993. Submit Form NZCO1 through the Online Companies Register, supplying the physical registered office address, directors' residential and service addresses, and share allocation details. Each director must consent to act using the RealMe authentication. Upload any bespoke constitution, or notify acceptance of the default statutory constitution, and pay the filing fee of NZD 105. The system will generate the Certificate of Incorporation automatically upon completion of the vetting, generally within 1-2 business days for straightforward submissions.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name validity search
Completed online Form NZCO1
Registered office physical street address (not P.O. Box)
Residential address and service address for each director
Signed consent to act as director
Shareholder schedule and initial share allocation
Company constitution (optional)
Payment of registration fee (NZD 105)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, request the Registrar's written reasons and submit a fresh name or obtain a section 23 consent from the conflicting registrant. If the application is queried due to data gaps, amend and resubmit within 5 working days. In the event of a suspension, an expedited corrective filing with the Companies Office toll-free service can restore processing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Corporate Constitution and Initial Share Allotment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors in harmony with the Companies Office (for constitution filing if desired)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene an inaugural board meeting to consider adoption of a constitution, either the default rules prescribed under the Companies Act 1993 or custom articles drafted by counsel. The constitution, if customised, must be signed by all subscribers and registered with the Companies Office within 10 working days after adoption under section 33. Following the constitutional adoption, the board resolves to allot the share capital to each subscriber in accordance with the subscription agreements. The company secretary must issue signed share certificates within 10 working days of allotment, complete the statutory share register, and maintain it for inspection under sections 84-87. If a subsequent allotment is made, file Form NZCO3 to update the register.
required_dossiers: Custom constitution (if adopted) or minute adopting default constitution
Board resolution allotting shares
Share subscription agreements
Proof of consideration received
Share certificate master and issued certificates
Form NZCO3 (statement of allotment) if filing is required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the constitution is rejected, revise the non-complying clauses in consultation with a corporate attorney and re-file within the statutory period. If the share allotment is challenged for inadequate consideration, provide the directors' valuation affidavit under section 36(2). Late filing of the constitution can be cured by a late application with explanation and possible late filing fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment and Registration of Directors and Company Secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that the company has at least one director who resides in New Zealand, as required by section 151(1) of the Companies Act 1993. If a foreign director is to be appointed, an exemption must be applied for and granted under section 151(3). Each director must execute a consent to act and the particulars must be filed with the Registrar using Form NZCO5 within 10 working days of the appointment. The board must also verify that no director is disqualified under the Act. If a company secretary is named, their written consent and residential address must be lodged as well. The Registrar will then update the online public register. This process ensures that legal process can be served promptly and that the company maintains good standing.
required_dossiers: Form NZCO5 (notice of director appointment)
Consent to act as director (original for each director)
Evidence of residency for the New Zealand-resident director
Exemption application for any non-resident director (if applicable)
Consent and details of company secretary (if appointed)
Copy of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If filing is declined for omission of information, correct the form and resubmit within 5 working days. If a director is disqualified or lacks the necessary residency, the board must immediately remove that director and appoint a compliant director, filing the revised certification. If an exemption is denied, an appeal can be lodged with the Registrar or a replacement director appointed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Banking Authorization, and Trade Participation Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), corporate banking provider, and New Zealand Customs Service (optional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the Inland Revenue Department for an IRD number using Form IR 596, and register for Goods and Services Tax (GST) if the value of taxable supplies will exceed NZD 60,000 in any 12-month period. For import/export of containers, also obtain a New Zealand Customs client code. The board must adopt a banking resolution authorising the opening of corporate accounts, the signatory limits, and the use of SWIFT Wire and ACH Debit rails. Certified copies of the Certificate of Incorporation, constitution, and board resolution, along with the directors' identification, must be submitted to the bank. After the account is opened, the company must also register for payroll (PAYE) if hiring employees, and obtain any separate insurance certificates. This step concludes the formation phase and enables operational trading.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Adopted constitution
Board resolution for bank account and authorised signatories
Passport and proof of address for each director
IRD forms IR596 and GST registration
Customs client code application (if applicable)
Bank account opening package and AML/KYC documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD number is delayed, follow up via the IRD business account and supply copies of the incorporation documentation. If the bank rejects the application under AML/CFT, provide enhanced KYC documents or apply to a different registered bank. If customs registration is pending, provide the border identification documentation to the Customs service desk and request expedited processing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Local Territorial Authority (District/City Council) under the Resource Management Act 1991; WorkSafe New Zealand under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015; Fire and Emergency New Zealand under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Resource Consent for Container Storage and Depot Operation; Trade Waste Discharge Permit; Hazardous Substances Compliance Certificate

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) of New Zealand
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B - Controlled Activity for small container depots (less than 500 TEU) requiring Resource Consent under section 88 of the RMA 1991; Category A - Full Environmental Impact Assessment under Schedule 4 of the RMA for depots exceeding 2,000 TEU or located near sensitive receptors. Purely leasing activities with no operational storage yard and using third-party depots may be Exempt from a full EIA, but the lessor must still maintain ISO container compliance and waste management records.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Washdown wastewater must have total suspended solids <50 mg/L and pH 6.0-9.0 before municipal sewer discharge under the trade waste bylaw. Stormwater runoff from container yards must be treated to reduce mineral oils to less than 15 mg/L. VOC emissions from degreasing activities must not exceed 0.25 mg/m3 as an 8-hour average, and hazardous waste such as refrigerants from reefer containers must be collected by an EPA-certified contractor and documented under the Waste Minimisation Act 2008.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire and Emergency New Zealand certification of the depot fire safety plan, including approved evacuation procedures and fire hydrant/standpipe inspection. Structural certification by a chartered professional engineer for container stacking racks and any gantry cranes, confirming compliance with AS/NZS 1170.1 structural loading and crane safety standards. WorkSafe New Zealand approval under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, including a site-specific Safe Work Method Statement (SWMS), hazard register, and documentation of employee training in container handling and confined space entry.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (New Zealand tax authority) and its myIR online portal; New Zealand Companies Office for NZBN/company registration; New Zealand Customs Service for export and border control.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity seeking a New Zealand Tax Identification Number (IRD number) must first determine whether it is required to register with the New Zealand Companies Office under the Companies Act 1993. For a non-resident entity carrying on a taxable activity in New Zealand, the steps are: (1) register for a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) where required; (2) submit the IRD non-resident registration application securely through myIR, attaching the certified overseas incorporation certificate, constitutional documents, foreign tax identification number, ultimate beneficial ownership schedule, director and secretary details, and either a New Zealand address for service or a New Zealand resident agent appointment; (3) obtain the IRD number from Inland Revenue, which is the New Zealand TIN and is also used as the GST registration number; (4) register for GST through myIR when taxable supplies made in New Zealand exceed or are expected to exceed NZD 60,000 within 12 months; (5) appoint tax representatives and file any required non-resident withholding tax registrations; and (6) retain the IRD confirmation notice and all myIR acknowledgements as conclusive registration evidence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - a standard New Zealand limited company is a separate taxable legal entity subject to New Zealand corporate income tax at 28%; it is not a pass-through entity in default form, but shareholder dividends may impute corporate tax credits.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No U.S.-style check-the-box election exists. Statutory elections available include the look-through company (LTC) election, tax consolidation election, and imputation group election; hybrid mismatch rules are applied under New Zealand domestic law with no elective opt-out.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in New Zealand in the past 12 months or reasonably expected in the next 12 months; compulsory GST registration applies above this threshold, with voluntary registration available below it.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No statutory real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory e-invoicing. GST is self-assessed and returns are filed through myIR; registered persons must issue compliant GST tax invoices, retain records, and may voluntarily use PEPPOL BIS Billing 3.0 e-invoicing.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under sections 11 and 11A of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, supplies of goods exported from New Zealand in the course of a taxable activity are zero-rated if the supplier holds satisfactory evidence of export. Services supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand are zero-rated if the services are not supplied in connection with New Zealand land or goods. For intermodal ISO shipping container leasing, cross-border leases of containers to non-resident shipping operators for use outside New Zealand can be zero-rated as exported goods or as offshore services to non-residents, while container leases for use within New Zealand are standard-rated at 15%. Zero-rated exporters claim a GST refund of attributable input tax through the myIR GST return; no separate refund form is required.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs Service electronic export declaration acknowledged through the New Zealand Trade Single Window
Bill of Lading or Sea Waybill showing container number, vessel, port of loading, port of discharge, and actual export date
Detailed commercial invoice and packing list describing the lessee, container identification, lease term, and lease/export proceeds

Foreign exchange receipt evidence, such as bank SWIFT credit advice, telegraphic transfer, foreign currency account statement, or overseas payment record showing receipt of proceeds from outside New Zealand
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may audit the entire export transaction, comparing the GST return, Customs export declarations, and bank receipts. If the zero-rating evidence package is missing, late, or inconsistent, the supply is reclassified as taxable at 15% GST and Inland Revenue may assess the unpaid GST, use-of-money interest, and shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 ranging from 20% for failure to take reasonable care up to 150% for evasion. False export declarations may also trigger penalties under the Customs and Excise Act 2018 and criminal liability under the Crimes Act 1961. Since New Zealand imposes no statutory 180-day foreign exchange repatriation deadline, the 180-day field is applied as the group's maximum evidence-package completion standard, after which zero-rating is no longer supported and records must be retained for seven years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) is the central bank and prudential supervisor under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989 and the Banking (Prudential Supervision) Act 2010; there is no separate foreign exchange control authority and RBNZ does not administer exchange-control permits or conversion licences.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains a fully convertible, floating New Zealand dollar and does not impose exchange controls on current or capital account transactions. The country has no surrender requirements for export receipts, no central bank conversion approval, and no restriction on the opening of foreign currency accounts by resident companies. Current account payments for leasing, charter hire, royalties, dividends, and service fees are freely executed by commercial banks once AML/CFT due diligence, tax withholding documentation, and a legitimate payment narrative are provided. Capital account flows, including equity injections, shareholder loans, acquisition of foreign assets, and repatriation of capital, are also free from RBNZ approval; investments that trigger sensitive-asset thresholds under the Overseas Investment Act need separate consent from the Overseas Investment Office inside MBIE. Profit remittance is not blocked, but New Zealand non-resident withholding tax and, for related parties, transfer pricing documentation must be handled. Banks must report suspicious transactions and large cash movements under the AML/CFT Act, but that is a supervisory reporting obligation rather than an exchange-control gate. Overall, the regime is best described as open, investor-friendly, and compatible with normal treasury liquidity planning.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio applies: New Zealand has no export surrender rule. Earners of foreign currency from leasing or any other export can lawfully hold 100% of proceeds in an onshore or offshore foreign currency account for an indefinite period, use them directly for foreign payables, or convert them at the market rate. The only practical controls are bank-level AML/CFT monitoring and the cross-border cash reporting threshold of NZD 10,000 for physical cash declarations under the Customs and Excise Act 2018.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Current Account with USD sub-account
Business Current Account and Foreign Currency Treasury Account
Corporate Operational Account with Import/Export Trade Finance Facility
Capital Escrow / Foreign Currency Deposit and FX Hedge Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech EMIs are not deposit-taking banks in New Zealand and cannot issue letters of credit or act as the principal escrow agent for capital injection where a New Zealand bank source is required. A foreign EMI may be registered as a money service business or financial service provider under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 and must carry AML/CFT obligations. From the treasurer's seat, the legal viability is medium-low: acceptable for non-critical payment rail or topping-up USD settlement with Wise/Airwallex-style platforms, but not for long-term liquidity clearing, LC issuance, or capital verification reports, all of which require a prudentially supervised New Zealand registered bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The Companies Act 1993 does not mandate physical attendance of directors at a bank branch. Under the AML/CFT Act banks may apply both face-to-face and non-face-to-face identification; remote consular-proxy opening is not a pure proxy right, because a bank still requires a direct interview or a previously verified electronic identity. For a new NZ private company with non-resident directors, Tier 1 banks generally require a video conference interview with at least one director and the treasury authorised signatory, plus certified copies (by a NZ notary, Justice of the Peace, or consular officer) of passports and proof of address. The bank may approve remote opening if the digital verification is based on trusted standards such as the New Zealand Digital Identity Trust Framework; where the directors lack such an identity, an in-branch appointment at an ANZ, ASB, BNZ, or Westpac branch is mandatory. A New Zealand registered office and company agent materially enhance onboarding speed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque non-resident corporate chain with discretionary trusts above the NZ shareholder, preventing the bank from identifying the ultimate beneficial owners within the standard 25% threshold.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a complete register of members and trust deeds or trust arrangements naming the settlor, protector, and beneficiaries; certificates of incorporation for each intermediary; certified passports and proof of residential address for all natural persons holding 10% or more beneficial interest; evidence of source of trust wealth; and a statutory declaration from the NZ director confirming no politically exposed person or sanctioned entity is hidden in the chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Directors reside overseas and cannot attend a New Zealand branch, so the bank is unable to match identity records to a biometric or government registry.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Secure digital identity verification through an accredited provider under the New Zealand Digital Identity Trust Framework; provide notarized or Justice of the Peace certified copies of passports and proof of address; undergo a recorded video interview with the bank; provide certified bank reference letters from each director's existing banking relationship; and attach a letter from the NZ company's chartered accountant confirming the identity assertions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value inbound capital injection of more than NZD 5 million intended to purchase containers, with a source of wealth that is difficult to evidence and that must be reconciled to share capital or shareholder loans.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit audited financial statements and bank statements of the investor for the last 24 months; container supply proforma invoice or sale and purchase agreement; independent valuation of the container fleet; business plan and projected lease cash flows; tax clearance from the investor's jurisdiction; and an undertaking to use a solicitors' trust account if funds originate from a loan facility.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lease revenue payments arrive from third-party payers rather than from the named lessees, creating layering and disproportionate payment reference risks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: File a written payment direction from each lease counterparty plus the underlying receivable assignment or novation agreement; provide bank statements showing reconciliation for each container lease contract; invoices, equipment handover certificates, insurance documents, and bills of lading; a reconciliation ledger matching payment reference codes to lease schedules; and a notarized declaration of beneficial ownership for each paying party.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The primary rail is an institutional SWIFT MT103 from the parent or shareholder bank to the NZD account of NZ Ltd. The remittance must identify the beneficiary company's NZ Companies Office number and the purpose statement 'Share subscription' or 'Paid-in capital - container fleet acquisition'. The bank may request the tax registration number, source of funds evidence, share allotment resolution, and board meeting minutes. After receipt, the company's chartered accountant issues a capital contribution confirmation, and the auditor can verify the bank statement against the share register. If the same transaction constitutes foreign investment in a sensitive sector, clearances under the Overseas Investment Act must be obtained before settlement. For foreign currency capital, a MT103 in USD or EUR can be credited to an onshore NZD account via an FX spot at the bank's treasury desk; alternatively, keep a USD sub-account and convert only the amount needed for local operating expenses.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements the following clearing rails are available: (1) SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfer, including SWIFT gpi, for lease security deposits, rental disbursements, and vendor payments below the LC threshold; (2) commercial letters of credit opened via SWIFT MT700 and advised by the beneficiary's bank, used when purchasing containers or fleet assets from overseas vendors; (3) documentary collections on D/P or D/A terms for lessees with acceptable country and sovereign risk; and (4) domestic NZD high-value clearing through Payments NZ HVCS for New Zealand counterparties. Each payment must carry the lease contract or invoice reference and a sanctions-compliant routing check of the beneficiary bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forward for NZD/USD with a registered New Zealand bank under an ISDA or NZFX master agreement, tenors aligned to underlying container lease receivables, permitted up to 100% of committed commercial exposure with no speculative overlay.
Vanilla FX options and collar structures for expected but non-contracted lease flows; maximum option tenor of 24 months and premium or collateral cost must be approved by the board.

Cross-currency interest rate swap (CCS) converting USD floating lease receipts into NZD fixed payments or vice versa, permitted for long-dated debt or lease contracts subject to bilateral ISDA and CSD credit support.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) only for third-country receivable currencies that are not deliverable under onshore settlement rules; NZD/USD should always be executed as a deliverable forward because New Zealand has full convertibility, and the NDF book must never create additional speculative exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of incorporation; statutory deadline is 31 working days after the incorporation anniversary.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZ$50.00; two consecutive unfiled annual returns trigger a notice of intention to remove the company from the New Zealand Companies Register, with administrative strike-off and dissolution completed 20 working days after notice unless an objection is filed; directors may be subject to disqualification for repeated non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 March balance date, the ordinary filing deadline is 7 July following the balance date; where an IRD-recognised tax agent extension is granted, the due date is 31 March of the following income year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties accrue at NZ$250 then up to NZ$500 per month; late payment interest is charged at the IRD prescribed rate (currently 8.30% per annum) on a daily compounding basis; persistent non-filing may lead to default tax assessments, debt enforcement, and prosecution with company-level fines up to NZ$50,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For monthly filers, due by the 28th day of the month following the taxable period; for two-monthly filers, due by the 28th day of the month following the two-month period; for six-monthly filers, due by the 28th day of the month following the six-month period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZ$200 per GST return; late payment interest at the IRD prescribed rate (currently 8.30% per annum) from the day after the due date; failure to file can result in default assessment and enforced recovery action, including garnishment and asset seizure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (prepared and made available to shareholders; audited and filed if the company is large)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies) for large companies; shareholders receive the financial statements.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after balance date (by 31 August for a 31 March balance date); if Registrar filing is required, deliver within 20 working days after the statements are provided to shareholders.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Every director in default is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding NZ$10,000 and a further NZ$500 for each day of continuing breach under the Companies Act 1993; a large company that persistently fails to file may be issued a remedial notice and subsequently struck off and dissolved.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand does not grant territorial tax holidays. Available reductions include the R&D Tax Incentive credit of 15% on qualifying R&D expenditure and capital allowances for the container fleet. No patent box regime exists. The general company tax rate is 28%, with no free-zone preferential rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 Company Income Tax Return, filed electronically through the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) myIR portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 is due by 7 July of the income year, or by 31 March of the following year where a tax agent extension is in force.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name, IRD number, and registered office details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact legal name of NZ Ltd and confirm incorporation in New Zealand. Non-resident shareholders and directors must be disclosed to IRD; use the IRD number registered to the company, not a foreign tax identification number, and ensure a physical New Zealand service address is on file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax agent details and contact information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Appoint a New Zealand tax agent to receive Notices of Assessment. Non-resident directors or offshore payment addresses should not be used as the company contact address. The agent must have authority to file the IR4 and deal with transfer-pricing documentation requests.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance date, accounting basis, and financial statement currency.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use NZ GAAP unless IRD accepts a foreign accounting standard. Convert all foreign currency container leasing revenue to NZD using IRD approved exchange rates at the balance date. Indicate whether accounts have been prepared for a standard 12-month period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit or loss before taxation per financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all gross leasing income from intermodal ISO shipping containers, including sub-leasing and ancillary demurrage, transportation, and container handling fees. For non-resident lessors, rental income from containers physically located in New Zealand is New Zealand-source. Also include any foreign-source income attributable to a New Zealand permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assessable income adjustments, exempt income, and depreciation recovered.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-assessable receipts or deduct exempt income. If a container is sold or retired, depreciation recovery is assessable. Non-resident-owned NZ companies do not obtain a territorial exemption; all global income is assessable unless a narrow domestic exclusion applies.

Add back entertainment expenditure, fines, penalties, and payments that are not for the purpose of deriving assessable income. Payments made to foreign related parties are not automatically deductible; if such payments are subject to non-resident withholding tax (NRWT), you must demonstrate that NRWT has been deducted and remitted at the correct statutory or treaty rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions for operating expenses, maintenance, depot storage, insurance, and financing costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only arm's length third-party depot storage, maintenance, repositioning costs, and insurance premiums. Intercompany lease management fees are deductible only if the fees are supported by transfer-pricing documentation and are paid under contracts that reflect economic substance. Interest deductions are subject to New Zealand thin-capitalisation rules where loans are owed to non-resident associates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Depreciation and capital allowances on the ISO container fleet.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the IRD prescribed depreciation rates for shipping containers leased under ISIC 5229 container leasing operations. Incoming or imported used containers must be valued on a cost basis adjusted for arm's length purchase price. No deduction is allowed for depreciation to the extent that the asset's cost exceeds open market value from an overseas related party.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Losses carried forward from prior years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct tax losses only if the company has maintained 49% shareholder continuity from the year the loss was incurred. For a non-resident-owned structure, a transfer of shareholding that changes ultimate foreign ownership during the year may extinguish loss carryforward. Complete the shareholder continuity schedule on the IR4 supplementary pages.

State the net amount to which the 28% company rate applies. This box must agree with the tax reconciliation statement. For a company wholly owned by non-residents, there is no ring-fencing election that changes entity-level taxability; the company is resident solely by incorporation and is taxed on its world-wide income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable at 28%, offsets, imputation credits, foreign tax credits, and R&D tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate the tax at 28% on Box 10. Attach the imputation credit account reconciliation. Claim foreign tax credits for taxes paid in treaty countries only if appropriate forms are attached. For the R&D tax credit, complete the IRD R&D supplementary form. Non-resident shareholders do not enter their shareholder tax details on this box; their tax arises only upon dividend distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: International tax schedules, transfer-pricing disclosure, and related-party transaction details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete IRD's International Questionnaire and transfer-pricing documentation index if cross-border related-party transactions exceed NZD 10 million. Disclose container lease arrangements with the foreign parent, offshore treasury, or marketing affiliates. State that contemporaneous Local File and Master File documentation is available for IRD inspection and identify each related party in the container leasing value chain.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the IR4 triggers a late filing penalty of NZD 250 for a company under the Tax Administration Act 1994 and an additional 10% of the tax shortfall if the return is not filed within 30 days after the IRD notice. Late payment penalties are 1% of unpaid tax immediately and 1% per month thereafter. Failure to maintain transfer-pricing documentation may lead to penalties up to NZD 20,000 plus an increase in shortfall penalties. Fraudulent evasion of income tax is punishable by a fine up to NZD 50,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% for non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) on dividends paid by a New Zealand company to non-resident shareholders, subject to reduction under an applicable New Zealand double tax agreement (DTA). A fully imputed dividend may qualify for a lower DTA rate such as 5% for a corporate shareholder holding at least 10% voting power.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the non-resident recipient must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home jurisdiction and provide it to the NZ company before the distribution is made. The recipient must complete the IRD reduced NRWT certificate form and certify that it is the beneficial owner of the dividend, interest, or royalty and is not a conduit or back-to-back nominee. The NZ payer must retain the TRC and beneficial ownership declaration in records and, where applicable, obtain an IRD approved reduced withholding rate certificate. If the protocol is not completed before payment, the payer must withhold at the statutory 30% dividend rate or the respective statutory interest/royalty rate and the recipient must later claim a foreign tax credit.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest paid to non-residents is subject to NRWT at 15%, or the approved issuer levy of 2% can apply to interest if the payer elects and the loan meets the IRD criteria. Royalties paid to non-residents are subject to statutory NRWT of 15%; under NZ DTAs royalties are commonly reduced to 10% or 5% depending on the country and IP involved. Interest may be reduced to 10% or 0% under certain treaty provisions, but the beneficial owner must file a treaty claim.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZD 10,000,000 in cross-border related-party transactions within the New Zealand entity triggers mandatory Local File preparation; a Master File is required where the multinational group has consolidated revenue exceeding NZD 1,100,000,000 and the New Zealand entity is a participant in the group.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not operate a UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime, but the Income Tax Act 2007 general anti-avoidance rules (s BG 1 and s GB 1) deny any tax advantage where an arrangement lacks commercial substance or has an avoidance purpose. For the container leasing entity, Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) should be located in New Zealand: acquisition and financing of the ISO container fleet, negotiation of lease terms, fleet utilisation management, maintenance scheduling, invoicing, credit control, and final acceptance of commercial risk. A structure that is a mere mailbox with no New Zealand staff or premises may be reconstructed and DTA benefits denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating intermodal container leasing revenue, inflating maintenance or depot deductions, diverting lease receipts to an affiliated off-balance sheet company, failing to file the IR4 return, or destroying leasing and depreciation records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Tax Administration Act 1994, ss 141A-141C, a shortfall penalty of up to 150% of the tax shortfall may be imposed for evasion or an arrangement with a dominant purpose of tax avoidance. Criminal prosecution under s 143A carries a fine up to NZD 50,000 and/or imprisonment up to 5 years. IRD may also issue a late filing penalty of NZD 250 and a 10% additional penalty on the unpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced when directors knowingly participate in the evasion. Directors may be personally liable for restitution of the diverted leasing revenue, subject to IRD departure prohibition orders and travel bans, and disqualified from managing companies under the Companies Act 1994. A director who signs a false return can be imprisoned for up to 5 years as a party to the offence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Thin Capitalisation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging a non-arm's length container lease rate to a foreign parent, paying excessive management or interest fees to a low-tax jurisdiction, and failing to prepare contemporaneous Local File, Master File, and thin-capitalisation calculations despite the NZD 10,000,000 related-party threshold being exceeded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: IRD may invoke Income Tax Act 2007 s GC 7 to substitute an arm's length consideration and disallow excessive interest under the thin-capitalisation rules in subpart FE. The associated shortfall penalty for an unacceptable tax position under TAA s 141B is up to 100% of the tax shortfall where reasonable care has not been exercised; if avoidance is the dominant purpose, the penalty escalates to 150%. Late payment penalties accrue at 1% per month.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly direct or implement the transfer-pricing scheme can be sued for the tax shortfall as accessaries. Civil orders may compel them to repay diverted intercompany lease profits, restore assets to the New Zealand company, and produce banking or wire transfer records. Repeated failure makes directors personally liable for corporate tax debts where they have knowingly allowed the company to trade while insolvent through artificial offshore fees.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT and Shell Company Economic Substance Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a pure shell company with no New Zealand premises, employees, or management; concealing the ultimate beneficial owner behind offshore nominees; accepting container lease payments by SWIFT or ACH from sanctioned counterparties; failing to perform anti-money-laundering customer due diligence on lessors or lessees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, failures to undertake customer due diligence or to report suspicious transactions can expose the company to penalties up to NZD 2,000,000. Violation of economic substance reconstruction under the Income Tax Act 2007 s BG 1 may be reconstructed by the Commissioner, and the company may be treated as not resident in New Zealand for treaty purposes, exposing all profits to tax with no treaty access.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be prosecuted for money laundering under the Crimes Act 1961 with imprisonment up to 7 years if they use the container leasing operations to conceal proceeds of crime. Shell company misuse also allows courts to pierce the corporate veil, making directors personally liable for the company's tax and AML penalties, freezing personal assets, issuing travel bans, and blacklisting the directors from acting as company officers in New Zealand.
